note: It is unknown whether every Euclid number is squarefree. The problem is listed as an open question in modern number theory literature, but the original source and year this problem was first posed could not be determined from available sources. Tietze (1965) documented Euclid numbers themselves (En = pn# + 1), and the problem likely arose after systematic study of their properties in the 1960s-1980s. A 2014 Mathematical Gazette article by Nick Lord proved the related but distinct property that Euclid numbers are power-free (not divisible by perfect squares of any prime).
